title: Children in Cages — Border Detention Facility Conditions
description_short: Children in Cages — Border Detention Facility Conditions
description_medium: In June 2018, journalists and lawmakers described children held in chain-link enclosures and crowded border facilities with limited bedding and hygiene supplies. A 2019 inspector-general report later found dangerous overcrowding at multiple sites. At least seven children died in federal custody between 2018 and 2019.
description_long: Reports from border facilities in June 2018 described children housed in chain-link enclosures, crowded rooms, and limited access to bedding and hygiene supplies. Journalists and members of Congress who visited the sites brought those conditions to wider public attention. A Department of Homeland Security inspector-general report in 2019 later found dangerous overcrowding at multiple locations. At least seven children died in federal custody between 2018 and 2019. DHS Secretary Kirstjen Nielsen disputed the use of the word “cages” for the enclosures as images and testimony circulated. The reports became part of the debate over the administration’s immigration enforcement and detention of children. Conditions varied across facilities; the reported findings do not establish that every child experienced the same treatment or that one site represented the entire system. The inspector-general findings and child deaths added scrutiny to federal oversight of children held in immigration custody.
